title: Communication Across Teams, Roles & Cultures
summary: Develop communication habits that support collaboration across different roles, departments, experiences, cultures, communication styles, and accessibility needs.
objectives: Explain why different roles may need different information.
Adapt communication without relying on stereotypes.
Recognize accessibility and inclusion as part of effective workplace communication.

vocab.def: Involving people from different roles, departments, or areas of expertise.
Communication designed to support participation, understanding, and respect across different people and needs.
Designing environments, information, tools, or communication so people with different abilities can participate effectively.
The transfer of responsibility, information, or work from one person or team to another.

sections.heading: Different roles need different context
sections.body: A manager, technician, customer, instructor, safety professional, or teammate may need different details from the same situation. Effective communication considers what each role needs to act responsibly.

sections.heading: Adapt without stereotyping
sections.body: People differ in communication preferences, language, experience, culture, and work style. Adapt based on the actual person and situation rather than assumptions about groups.

sections.heading: Accessibility is part of communication quality
sections.body: Communication may need captions, interpretation, readable formatting, visual alternatives, plain language, assistive technology, additional processing time, or another reasonable accommodation.

sections.heading: Good handoffs protect continuity
sections.body: When work moves between people or teams, the receiving person should receive enough accurate information to understand status, risks, decisions, unfinished work, and next steps.

practice.prompt: You are handing unfinished work to another shift. What information should you provide?
practice.answer: Provide the current status, completed work, unfinished work, known risks or issues, important decisions, and next steps.

practice.prompt: A teammate uses an accommodation or communication method that is different from yours. What should guide your response?
practice.answer: Use the agreed accessible communication method and focus on effective participation rather than assumptions.

quiz.question: What best supports communication across different teams and roles?
options: Provide accurate context appropriate to the receiver while respecting accessibility and individual needs
Give every person exactly the same information in exactly the same format
Assume people from the same background communicate the same way
Leave important information out of handoffs to keep messages short
quiz.answer: Provide accurate context appropriate to the receiver while respecting accessibility and individual needs

lab.objective: Create a cross-team handoff that communicates status, risks, decisions, unfinished work, accessibility considerations, and next steps.
